Our primary goal is to provide opportunities for students to learn about machine intelligence in a community environment. Our secondary goal is to increase interdepartmental and multi-university interaction relevant to machine intelligence — to bring those interested in machine intelligence closer together.

We aim to strengthen relationships between Black athletes across teams, engage with organizations in the greater Boston area, and promote opportunities that support the academic, athletic, and personal success of our members. Through collaboration and advocacy, we seek to increase Black representation in MIT Athletics and provide a unified voice for Black student-athletes within the athletic department.

name: MIT Asian American Initiative
description: The Asian American Initiative strives, through action and education, to promote Asian American advocacy on the MIT campus and beyond. Our club aims to provide a safe space to discuss the building blocks and facets of Asian American identity, create a platform to bring light to issues affecting the Asian American community, and improve the Asian American experience on and off campus, while supporting other marginalized groups. name: MIT Azerbaijani Students Association
description: The purpose of the MIT Azerbaijani Students Association is to promote awareness and appreciation of Azerbaijani culture, history, and contemporary developments within the MIT community. The organization aims to create a welcoming and inclusive environment for Azerbaijani students, as well as for all members of the MIT community interested in learning about Azerbaijan and the broader Caucasus region. Through cultural, educational, and social events, the association will foster meaningful cross-cultural exchange and community engagement. The organization also seeks to build connections with Azer

name: MIT Ballet Theatre
description: A primary purpose of the MIT Ballet Theatre is to produce and stage ballets for the greater MIT community. These ballets provide an opportunity for students to audition for and perform. MIT Ballet Theatre will show at least one ballet or dance concert (in the style of ballet) every semester. Works may either be existing or student-choreographed ballets. The concert or ballet will contribute to culture and entertainment to the MIT community and give students a chance to express themselves and connect with the world around them through choreography. name: MIT Bridge Club
description: To provide a platform for bridge lovers to play bridge weekly. To teach bridge to those who are interested.

name: MIT Capital Partners
description: MIT Capital Partners provides students with exposure to and preparation for careers in startups and venture capital, while fostering a diverse, supportive community. Through educational programming, mentorship, and real-world experiences, members gain a deeper understanding of how startups grow and how investors make decisions.

name: MIT Climbing Team
description: The purpose of the MIT Climbing Team is to develop a community of undergraduate and graduate students who want to reach an advanced level of rock climbing. We support students by providing structured practices and goal-oriented training programs. Our goals are to give this community access to formal training, affordable climbing facilities, and opportunities to participate in formal competitions and fun outdoor activities.

name: MIT Club Peru
description: The mission of MIT Club Peru is to expand our culture and help fellow Peruvians by providing Peruvian students on campus with the ability to unite and support each other, providing a source of cultural fulfillment by organizing outings and social bonding events, and providing non-Peruvian students/allies an immersion into Peruvian culture.

name: MIT Colombian Association
description: The MIT Colombian Association is a student-led organization recognized by MIT's Association of Student Activities (ASA). Our purpose is to share the Colombian culture at MIT and the Greater Boston Area, to bring together the Colombian MIT community, to organize academic and non-academic events with other student associations, to strengthen relationships between academia and policymakers in Colombia interested in the fields of study promoted by MIT, and to foster the connection between MIT and Colombia.

name: MIT Democrats
description: MIT Democrats represents politically engaged members of the MIT community, including students, staff, faculty, and alumni, who generally support Democratic candidates for office, the advancement of progressive ideals in American politics, and the improvement of the Democratic Party.

name: MIT Divest
description: Our goal is to get MIT to cut all ties with the fossil fuel industry, including but not limited to funding, research influence, and recruitment!

name: MIT Energy and Climate Club
description: The MIT Energy and Climate Club connects students, alumni, and community members who are passionate about energy and climate change. From 2004 to 2024, the Energy Club has been MIT's central platform for discussions about energy at the world's leading technical institute. In the Fall of 2021, we expanded our work to include not only energy but also the fight to combat climate change, and the intersection of these two subject areas. As the club with the largest reach on campus, we are a hub for thought-leadership and relationship building. Join our powerful community today.

name: MIT Entrepreneurship Club
description: We provide MIT students with a community of students who are currently founders or are dedicated to become founders at some point in the future. Additionally, we help connect MIT students passionate about entrepreneurship to opportunities to further their career in the world of startups.

name: MIT Every Nation Campus (ENC)
description: Welcome to Every Nation Campus – where open minds meet open hearts. We're a discussion-based Christian group open to all. Rejecting clichés, we dive into life's toughest questions while embracing our creativity. We believe in a God who made us not just to think, but to create, enjoy and have fun. Join us for lively discussions, warm fellowship, and weekly dinners.

name: MIT Farm
description: The purpose of MIT Farm is to promote hands-on farming and gardening across MIT’s campus and the broader region. We engage members through community volunteering, growing workshops, food production initiatives, and social gatherings centered on sustainable agriculture.

name: MIT Film Makers Association
description: MIT Film Makers Association provides unprecedented opportunities of film production and artistic expression for MIT students, staff and alumni. We are a welcoming and loving community for cinephiles, movie critics, filmmakers and potential filmmakers at MIT, Harvard, and all other colleges/schools around Boston. We provide opportunities for members to create films, meet other creators, and learn more about filmmaking through events and workshops.

name: MIT Flow
description: Flow is a traditional Chinese dance team on MIT’s campus, established Fall 2023. We are dedicated to exploring and sharing the beauty of Chinese traditional, ethnic, and folk dance styles. Our goals are to provide a supportive community on MIT’s campus to learn diverse styles, as well as share traditional Chinese dance through performances within the MIT community and the greater Boston area.

name: MIT Gala
description: The MIT Gala is a space to celebrate visual arts at MIT through an end-of-year event with a runway and art gallery, as well as supporting those in the MIT community interested in fashion through the process of designing and fabricating a piece to be shown off on the runway.

name: MIT Georgian Society
description: Our mission is to raise awareness about Georgia and Georgian culture.

name: MIT German Club
description: MIT German Club is a club dedicated to bringing together those who share an interest in the German language and culture.

name: MIT Global Health Alliance
description: The ultimate mission of the MIT Global Health Alliance is to educate and advocate for health equity and social justice in a global context. We aim to do so via partnerships with local and international organizations and community educational campaign efforts. In particular, we engage with the community through boothing on MIT’s campus, hosting global health-related courses for MIT Educational Studies Programs, organizing panels with experts in the field, and biweekly presentations given to our club general body. To witness that the Lord Jesus Christ is God Incarnate, and to seek to lead others to personal faith in Christ as Lord and Savior. This goal shall be accomplished through music, arts, and personal communications. b. To help Christians grow toward maturity as disciples of Christ by encouraging them to find a church home, by study of the bible, by prayer, and by Christian Fellowship. name: MIT Graduate Women's Reading Group
description: The purpose of the MIT Graduate Women’s Reading Group (GWRG) is to foster intellectual connection, cross-disciplinary dialogue, and a sense of belonging among MIT students through a monthly, member-driven reading community. The group was founded to address the particular isolation that graduate students—especially women—can experience in the department- and lab-centric structure of graduate life at MIT. name: MIT Guild of Bellringers
description: The purpose of the Guild is to promote and perpetuate the art of bell ringing and to provide an opportunity for its members to participate and improve in the group ringing of handbells and tower bells when welcomed.

name: MIT Informatics Tournament Club
description: We, the members of the MIT Informatics Tournament Club (M(IT)^2), in order to spearhead initiatives for the M(IT)^2 tournament, to foster a worldwide community of competitive programmers anchored at MIT, to establish a fair system of appointing leadership, to host programming classes for the MIT community, and to give all members a voice in organizational matters, hereby ordain and institute this Constitution.

name: MIT Iranian Association
description: To promote fellowship amongst students who are from Iran or are interested in Persian culture, through social and cultural events. To introduce Persian culture and traditions to the MIT community. Raise awareness of the social and civil occurrences in Iran.

name: MIT Israel Alliance
description: The purpose of the MIT Israel Alliance is to promote and advocate for the safety and freedom of the Jewish people, as well as the State of Israel, through educative action and cultural events within MIT and throughout Massachusetts. The MIT Israel Alliance will promote the above goal as consistent with MIT Policies Regarding Student Behavior and all applicable law.

name: MIT Latin Dance Club
description: To build a community of people who like Latin Dancing!

name: MIT Library for Underrepresented Narratives and Archives
description: The purpose of LUNA is to create space for the promotion, discussion, and distribution of literature by authors from marginalized and/or underrepresented communities. We seek to create a space that affirms people of marginalized cultures, identities, and orientations through access to literature. We also seek to gestate political organization, awareness, and activism.

name: MIT LIVE
description: MIT LIVE aims to provide a platform for MIT student musicians to arrange music, rehearse together, perform live, and showcase their talents. We welcome a variety of genres and instruments. Member can see their vision come to fruition through the delivery of a song during our end-of-semester showcases. Members may wish to start side projects, such as cover videos, original compositions, street performances, etc. and we will support them with our resources.

name: MIT Minority Association of Pre-Medical Students
description: The mission of the Minority Association of Pre-Medical Students (M.A.P.S.) shall be to address the needs of the minority pre-health students at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. M.I.T.M.A.P.S. intends to motivate, encourage and prepare pre-health students from a disadvantaged background, an underrepresented minority group or a medically underserved area to be competitive applicants for health professional schools through a sharing of knowledge, experience and mentorship. The chapter is dedicated to serving underserved communities through a variety of community service activities and v

name: MIT Model United Nations
description: The mission of the MIT Model United Nations club is to create opportunities for students to develop their professional debate and research skills, applied in an engaging political and social context.

name: MIT Nordic Club
description: The MIT Nordic Club aims to bring together Nordic students at MIT, foster a sense of community, and celebrate the Nordic cultures through events and gatherings.

name: MIT Nritya
description: MIT Nritya's mission is to foster a collaborative environment for Indian Classical Dance enthusiasts on campus to bond over their shared passion for dance. We hope to showcase the group's talent both through performances on campus and performances in the Greater Boston Area (and beyond) for the broader community.

name: MIT Pre-Law Society
description: The MIT Pre-Law Society provides pre-law students with opportunities, resources, and a collaborative community to succeed in law school and legal careers. As one of MIT’s only law-focused student groups, we support aspiring lawyers through networking events, law school application assistance, and professional development initiatives.

name: MIT QuestBridge Scholars Network
description: The MIT QuestBridge Scholars Network (QSN) Chapter is affiliated with QuestBridge (QB), a national non-profit organization that connects high-achieving, low-income high school students with admission and full scholarships to the nation’s best colleges. MIT’s QSN Chapter strives to create a supportive, engaging, and welcoming community for our 230+ QuestBridge Scholars who we often call Questies! Throughout the year, we arrange social events, foster friendships, and provide on-campus resources and mentorship.

name: MIT ROTC Association
description: The MIT ROTC Association (MIT ROTCA) is dedicated to fostering a unified community for MIT students involved in ROTC across all programs. Our mission is to provide a student-led, cross-branch support network that promotes leadership development, mentorship, and camaraderie among cadets and midshipmen. MIT ROTCA serves as a bridge between ROTC students and the broader MIT community, facilitating interdisciplinary discussions, professional development opportunities, and outreach initiatives that enhance civil-military engagement on campus. name: MIT Running Club
description: Group runs along the Charles.

name: MIT Saudi Students Association
description: Supporting the holistic growth of Saudi students by advocating for their needs, celebrating our heritage, and providing essential resources for academic and professional success

name: MIT Science Policy Review
description: The MIT Science Policy Review is a researcher-run publication founded in 2019 whose primary purpose is to publish accessible and authoritative science policy reviews authored by members of the broader scientific community for dissemination to the wider public. Additionally, the MIT Science Policy Review aims to be a resource for local, state, federal, and international policymakers who are involved in the creation and funding of science policies, especially those that are highly technical in subject matter. name: MIT Student Events Board
description: We are the Student Events Board: MIT's main fun factory. We work with SOLE and other admin offices to organize the largest events on campus. If you have ever heard of SpringFest or Tech Twinkles: We make it happen! The Board has 21 members, including 5 officers. Any undergraduate or graduate student is welcome to join.

name: MIT Student Veterans Association
description: To provide a supportive community for veterans and service members at MIT through direct advocacy, disseminating helpful information, and hosting social events.

name: MIT Sustainability Summit
description: To convene a diverse range of leaders – from industry, academia, and students – and leverage MIT's unique interdisciplinary strengths to address pressing sustainability challenges. Through collaboration and innovation, the Summit aims to empower participants to design and implement solutions that ensure a just, equitable, and thriving future for both humanity and the planet.

name: MIT Undergraduate Association
description: MIT's undergraduate student government.

name: MIT Wind Club
description: The purpose of the MIT Wind is to promote wind energy education and outreach within MIT and in the greater Boston community. The goal educational component of MIT Wind is to prepare students with the skills and connections to enter the wind energy industry. For undergraduate members, the centerpiece of MIT Wind is participation in the Department of Energy Collegiate Wind Competition (CWC), an annual event in which the objective is to build an operational model turbine to compete against other collegiate teams. name: MITALY - Italian Student Association
description: At MITaly, we are a vibrant community of Italian students and scholars at MIT, united by a shared heritage and a passion for connection. Our mission is to celebrate and promote Italian culture, traditions, and values within the MIT ecosystem through social gatherings, cultural festivities, and academic networking. We strive to create a supportive environment where members can feel at home, forge lasting friendships, and collaborate across disciplines. By honoring our roots and embracing diversity, we aim to build bridges between Italy and the global MIT community.

name: MITap
description: MITap is a tap company dedicated to spreading the art of tap dance on MIT’s campus and across the Boston/Cambridge area. We are committed to training in tap technique and performing tap dance.

name: MITeri
description: 1. To strengthen the Nepali community within MIT and the bigger Boston area 2. To celebrate with and represent Nepali culture and traditions to MIT community members.

name: MITVote
description: MITvote is a nonpartisan group of graduates and undergraduates with the goal of engaging an active voter community on campus. Our mission is to make voting as accessible as possible for everyone and encourage civic participation on MIT's campus.

name: MITxHarvard Women in AI
description: We are a club of MIT and Harvard students who are interested in artificial intelligence and machine learning. We use an inclusive definition of the word women, and the purpose of the Women in Artificial Intelligence group is to provide a supportive community for cisgender women, transgender women, genderqueer women and individuals, and non-binary individuals pursuing studies or research in AI and machine learning at MIT and Harvard.

name: MIXED
description: To provide a community for students who are of a mixed heritage and experience. We aim to create space for students to embrace their cultures and the complexities of the intersection of multiple identities, to increase awareness of the diversity of the mixed experience, and to discuss mixed issues.

name: Mocha Moves Dance Squad
description: Established in 1999, Mocha Moves is an MIT-based dance team whose mission is to be a creative outlet for members to develop their skills. We share our talent and passion for dance by hosting performances, such as Ring the Alarm and Mocha Show, and participating in many others hosted throughout the Greater Boston Area. We strive to learn and grow together by cultivating our talents and connections with the Boston dance community. On Mocha, the grind never stops!

name: Mock Trial Team
description: MIT Mock Trial is a student organization which competes under the American Mock Trial Association (AMTA). Members develop skills in public speaking, debate, legal understanding, acting, and more through tournaments throughout the year.

name: Mongolian Student Association
description: Mongolian Students Association's mission is to promote Mongolian culture at MIT. We’re determined to bring Mongolian students closer together and to support them through their journey at MIT, helping them through many challenges such as culture shock and homesickness.

name: moveMENtality
description: The purpose of the moveMENtality is to create a space for male-identifying students to experiment with and explore dance at MIT. Our membership is composed of students who are interested in dance, whether or not they have had dance experience before college. We choreograph and practice a new performance each semester, and perform at showcases such as Ring the Alarm, Footwork, and DT Shows.

name: Mujeres Latinas
description: We are a group at MIT who focus on creating community for other Latinas at MIT. We want to promote service, knowledge, and identity to our community.

name: Muses
description: The MIT Muses are an all-treble a cappella group comprised of students (both undergraduate and graduate) at MIT. The Muses sing a minimum of two concerts per year: one during the fall and another in the spring. Additionally we perform in two campus-wide performances each year, the Fall family weekend concert and the Spring CPW concert. We also sing at various gigs both on and off campus throughout the year. The Muses also do an annual fundraiser on Valentine’s Day in which we serenade various members of the MIT community.

name: Music Production Collaborative
description: We promote the collaboration, education, and exchange of ideas among MIT community members interested in all aspects of music production.

name: Musical Theatre Guild
description: The MIT Musical Theatre Guild is the oldest and largest theatre organization at MIT, and we are entirely student-run! Formed from the merger of the MIT Gilbert and Sullivan Society, the Classical Musical Society, and the Tech Show Society in 1971, we produce a wide variety of Musical Theatre. We perform four shows a year so there is plenty of opportunity to act, sing, dance, tech, design, direct, and produce. So, if you want to be part of a great art form, come investigate MTG!

name: Muslim Students Association
description: The MIT Muslim Student Association (MSA) seeks to foster a welcoming, spiritually enriching, and intellectually vibrant community for Muslims and non-Muslims alike at MIT. We are dedicated to supporting the religious, academic, and personal development of students through inclusive programming that reflects the values of Islam. Our mission is to cultivate meaningful spaces for worship, dialogue, learning, and social engagement, while striving to build bridges of understanding between Muslims and the broader MIT community. name: National Society of Black Engineers
description: To increase the number of culturally responsible Black Engineers who excel academically, succeed professionally and positively impact the community

name: Native American & Indigenous Association
description: The Native American & Indigenous Association seeks to provide social, political, cultural and academic support for Massachusetts Institute of Technology undergraduate and graduate students of Native American descent and Native student allies. name: Next Act
description: The purpose of Next Act shall be to produce and present an annual full-length musical production during MIT’s Campus Preview Weekend (CPW) and to serve as a portal into the world of musical theater for veterans and beginners alike. Anyone who auditions for a Next Act production is guaranteed to be cast in a speaking and/or singing role, regardless of experience.

name: Next Sing
description: The mission of Next Sing is to provide a fun, noncompetitive, low commitment music activity for all MIT students interested in music. We welcome all musicians––singers and instrumentalists, undergrads and grad students––to join! We accept people of all skill levels and backgrounds. Our musical acts all involve vocalists and sometimes instrumentalists.

name: Open Discourse Society
description: The purpose of the MIT Open Discourse Society (MODS) is to cultivate civil discourse and intellectual diversity within the MIT community. MIT is the global STEM epicenter, and for so long, advancements in science and technology here and elsewhere have stemmed from the willingness to engage in productive discussions and good-faith evaluation of ideas. MODS aims to recreate environments where such discussions and evaluation are the norm and devoid of bigoted obloquy. name: OrigaMIT
description: The purpose of OrigaMIT is to provide current origami artists a place to meet others who share the same passion, and to provide new or interested folders an opportunity to learn.

name: Origins
description: Our mission at MIT Origins is to foster holistic well-being within the MIT community by offering a diverse range of activities, including yoga, Vedic spiritual wisdom, nourishing dinners, spiritual festival celebrations, enriching workshops, engaging weekly discussions, retreats, and more. We are committed to nurturing the body, mind, and spirit, guiding individuals towards greater fulfillment and balance in their lives.

name: Orthodox Christian Fellowship of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
description: Our mission is 1) to be the loving presence of Christ and the Orthodox Christian Church on college campuses, 2) to be an integral part of students’ spiritual formation by challenging them to explore the Faith, 3) to inspire students to commit to living an Orthodox Christian way of life daily.

name: Outing Club
description: The purpose of MITOC shall be to create a safe community around outdoor recreation and to provide students with the education and means to use, enjoy, and explore the great outdoors.

name: Palestine at MIT
description: At Palestine@MIT, we are dedicated to promoting the Palestinian heritage, tradition and culture. We embrace our identity and our values are rooted in the our rich history of striving for freedom and liberation. We believe we own tomorrow. Tomorrow is a Palestinian day.

name: Pediatric Hope Project
description: The purpose of Pediatric Hope Project at MIT is to provide free tutoring and educational support to children with cancer and other serious illnesses whose schooling has been disrupted. The organization represents a chapter of the National Pediatric Hope Project organization and will partner with local hospitals and community programs to deliver one-on-one tutoring, small group sessions, and educational workshops. description: The Phi Kappa Psi Fraternity is an association of men of integrity who strive to develop the individual in his intellect, in his involvement in the community, and in his faith. Recognizing and valuing the diversity of all, the Fraternity unites the principles and traditions of our past with the resources and creativity of our present to provide an environment in which our members can realize their highest potential. To this end, we offer a lifelong experience, guided by our faith in a power greater than ourselves, in contributing to the betterment of both the individual and the community.

description: PLEASURE is a student group at MIT supported by the Violence Prevention & Response (VPR) office and the Office for Student Wellbeing (OSW) that aims to improve how our communities navigate sex and relationships in order to end sexual and all forms of identity-based violence through peer education.

name: Pokemon League
description: The purpose of MIT Pokémon League is to (1) promote an MIT student community that appreciates and plays a variety of Pokémon games and (2) establish a Pokémon League at MIT, which will be officially recognized by the Play! Pokémon organization.

name: Poker Club
description: The purpose of this club is to create a community with like interests and also create a better understanding in the game of poker.

name: Pokerbots
description: Pokerbots' main purpose is to run the annual MIT Pokerbots class and competition during IAP, including teaching all of our students and securing sponsorship funding for the competition prizes.

name: Polish Club
description: Bringing Polish culture and community to MIT – celebrating traditions, fostering connections, and sharing opportunities for cultural engagement.

name: Polymer Graduate Student Association
description: The mission of the Polymer Graduate Student Association (hereafter referred to as PGSA) is to facilitate social and academic interaction among PPSM (Program in Polymer Science and Soft Matter) students, as well as promote the well-being and vitality of the program to maintain its status as a forum for interdepartmental polymer research.

name: PreMedical Society
description: Foster community within pre-health students at MIT and prepare members for a career in medicine.

name: ProLife
description: The MIT Pro-Life Club is focused on spreading awareness about the risks about abortion, about the philosophies against abortion, providing resources to women who are considering getting, currently getting, or have gotten an abortion. The MIT Pro-Life Club is also focused on working with local and national organizations that assist in the aforementioned efforts.

name: Puzzle Club
description: The purpose of the organization is to promote interest and participation in puzzles on campus, through solving and writing puzzles, as well as running various events and meetings throughout the year. The flagship event is the annual MIT Mystery Hunt (“the Hunt”), a weekend long activity held during IAP in which teams of participants compete to solve a variety of puzzles and find a coin hidden on campus.

name: Quiz Bowl Team
description: The MIT Quiz Bowl Team is an organization of MIT undergraduate and graduate students who compete in and host academic trivia (i.e. quizbowl) competitions. The purpose of the MIT Quiz Bowl Team is to promote and encourage participation in quiz bowl events, academic competitions, and trivia games, and the accumulation of trivial knowledge; to host on-campus and interscholastic quiz bowl tournaments; and to recruit, train, and support the quiz bowl teams which represent MIT in intercollegiate competition.

name: Radio Society W1MX
description: The purpose of the Society shall be to gather together the students of MIT having an interest in amateur radio. The Society will endeavor to maintain an HF (Below 30MHz) Amateur Radio Station for the use of its members, both in individual activities and with the intent of promoting the image of MIT throughout the world via amateur radio.

name: Reformed University Fellowship
description: RUF is a community that is committed to considering the good news of Jesus together. We seek to be an authentic community that is supportive, spiritually challenging, and outward facing to our peers on campus. RUF is a safe place to ask questions, voice doubts and explore Christianity with other students at MIT.

name: Resonance of MIT
description: The purpose of The Resonance of MIT is to provide an outlet to sing a cappella non-competitively at MIT. The Resonance will strive to maintain a low key and fun atmosphere. We will keep required time commitment to such a level as to allow members to be active participants in other activities (especially performance groups) at MIT.

name: Ribotones
description: The MIT Ribotones is a music service group that aims to use music as a means of community service in the greater Boston community and beyond. We are string/piano/wind players, vocalists, and chamber groups (e.g., trios, quartets, sextets, octets) who love to play volunteer recitals at local venues such as hospitals, nursing homes, long-term care facilities, and more, delivering quality music to the residents. Our primary goal is to bring the joy of music free of charge to those who may have limited access to live performances, no matter their prior experience with music.

name: Ridonkulous
description: Established in spring 2005, Ridonkulous is an urban dance crew whose goal is to bring MIT dance to other venues in the greater Boston area and to express our passion and commitment to teamwork and dance. In addition to performing at charity events, collegiate showcases, and competitions across the Greater Boston area, we host our own annual showcase, Footwork. Our mission is to have fun, dance, and show the world why we are so RIDONKULOUS!

name: Roadkill Buffet
description: An Improv Comedy troupe which exists to bring joy to the MIT community through our public and free performances, as well as to improve and enhance the craft of our troupe members.

name: Rocket Team
description: We will design, build, test, launch, and recover a rocket — flying an engaging scientific experiment — beyond the Kármán Line.

name: Sangam

Providing forums for both learned and casual discussion of issues relevant to the subcontinent and the people whose roots are there. 3. Working with MIT and our partner organizations to ensure that the total needs of the General Sangam Body are met.

name: Scholars of Finance
description: The purpose of the Scholars of Finance is to develop the next generation of highly capable financial executives, who will act and lead from a strong grounding in principles and ethics.

name: Science Bowl
description: The purpose of MIT Science Bowl is to promote science education and exposure to the K-12 community via the organization of at least two buzzer-style competitions. These competitions are the Fall Invitational, catering to high-school teams across the nation, and the Spring Regional, the official National Science Bowl regional competition for the Northeast Region.

name: Science Club for Girls at MIT
description: The mission of Science Club for Girls at MIT is to foster excitement, confidence, and literacy in STEM for girls and gender-expansive youth from underrepresented communities by providing free, experiential programs and by maximizing meaningful interactions with women-in-STEM mentors. Girls work with mentor-scientists who model and foster leadership and promote careers in science and technology as goals and options. name: SIAM
description: The purpose of the MIT SIAM (Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics) chapter is to engage the diverse MIT community with a shared interest in Applied Mathematics and Computational Science. We seek to further SIAM’s mission to bridge the world of mathematics with that of science and technology. Our group aims to encourage interdisciplinary collaboration, and facilitate exchange of ideas and scientific results.

name: Smash UltiMIT
description: The purpose of Smash UltiMIT is to maintain a centralized community of competitive Super Smash Bros players by hosting tournaments.

name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
description: SHPE (Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers) is a nonprofit organization serving and advancing Hispanics in STEM. With more than 13,000 student and professional members, SHPE’s mission is to change lives by empowering the Hispanic community to realize its fullest potential and to impact the world through STEM awareness, access, support, and development. To accomplish this, SHPE provides a variety of programming, services, resources, and events, including hosting the largest Hispanic STEM convention in the nation.

name: Society of Physics Students
description: To provide information and service in the interest of the members of MIT community who are interested in physics and to encourage interaction between undergraduate students, graduate students, faculty, staff, and other members of MIT community interested in physics.

name: Society of Women Engineers
description: MIT Society of Engineers was founded in 1979. Since then, MIT SWE has strived to inspire younger generations about engineering, encourage the notion of diversity in engineering, and determine and advocate for the needs of women engineers at MIT and the broader community.

name: Somali Student Association
description: The Somali Student Association (SSA) exists to build community at MIT around Somali culture, language, and scholarship. The association will organize educational forums, cultural programs, and service initiatives that highlight the diversity of Somalia and its diaspora while supporting students’ academic and professional growth.

name: South Asian Association of Students
description: MIT's South Asian Association of Students (SAAS) is one of the largest groups on campus, dedicated to promoting South Asian culture and creating spaces for students of South Asian descent at MIT. SAAS is open to all students interested in getting a taste of South Asian culture. Our organization was founded with the purpose of celebrating the diversity of South Asian culture and providing spaces for discourse and community among people with ties to that culture. description: The purpose of the SSA is to be a home for all students with either an interest in South Slavic culture and history, or students with a South Slavic background interested in connecting with other South Slavs. The SSA aims to connect the many American South Slavs, International South Slavic students, as well as friends and generally interested students in the culture. The group will work to be a source of connection in a network of such students and promote student mental health and interaction the through organization of cultural events. name: Spain at MIT
description: To bring the Spaniards at MIT together, and to share their culture with the rest of the MIT community

name: Spinning Arts Club
description: The purpose of the MIT Spinning Arts Club is to provide students with a venue in which to learn and practice prop spinning for both fire and glow props, as well as access to instruction in both performance and safety with fire.

name: Sport Taekwondo Club
description: To provide a community to promote wellness, health, and taekwondo excellence among club members.

name: Sporting Clays Association
description: The MIT Sporting Clays Association is a competitive shotgun shooting team. We practice on flying targets in the disciplines of Skeet, Trap, and Sporting Clays. The sport takes a tremendous amount of discipline and helps members to improve their mental focus as well as hand-eye coordination. Additionally, the club teaches its members how to safely and respectfully handle firearms while introducing them to a sport that plays a significant role in American culture.

name: Squash Club
description: MIT Squash Club is a vibrant community dedicated to promoting squash for all members of the MIT community. Whether you’ve played your whole life or have never picked up a racket, our club offers amazing opportunities to compete, improve your skills, and build community.

name: Stand-Up CoMITy
description: The purpose of Stand-Up CoMITy is to promote student mental health and wellbeing through comedy, as well as provide a platform for students and staff to ideate, write, and perform stand-up comedy as a means of self-expression.

name: StartLabs
description: Foster the next generation of technical entrepreneurs by helping MIT students learn about startups and launch innovative ventures.

name: Strategic Games Society
description: At MIT SGS (Strategic Games Society), our mission is to unite board game enthusiasts from MIT and the Boston-Cambridge area. Our focus lies in having fun, fostering connections, and ensuring that MIT SGS continues to be the longest-standing board game club at MIT. We meet twice weekly: Fridays at 6:05PM and Sundays at 3:05PM. Please join our Discord Server (https://discord.gg/73TESWpfQM) and/or our mailing list (https://mailman.mit.edu/mailman/listinfo/sgs-members) for weekly announcements.

name: Student Information Processing Board
description: Our mission is to provide students with improved access to computational facilities; to serve as an advocate for the MIT Community to the Faculty and the Administration in computer-related topics; to function as an information center for members of the MIT Community interested in topics in computer science or computing; to conduct, manage, and support experiments run by students to advance the techniques of organization, planning, and administration of access to computers; and to initiate, develop, and provide computer services deemed valuable to the MIT Community.

name: Student Juggling Club
description: 1. To educate students about the art of juggling. 2. To provide students with the chance to learn from other jugglers.

name: Student Sustainability Coalition
description: Established in the summer of 2020, the Student Sustainability Coalition (SSC) congregates student sustainability-related groups at MIT, facilitating communication, collaboration, and collective action. Given the diversity of student sustainability organizations and opportunities on campus, we aim to act as a centralized overarching organization, making connections between groups and elevating the student voice.

name: Students for the Exploration and Development of Space
description: SEDS is an independent, student-based, student-run organization which promotes the exploration and development of space. SEDS pursues this mission by educating people about the benefits of space, by supporting a network of interested students, by providing an opportunity for members to develop their leadership skills, and inspiring people through our involvement in space-related projects. SEDS believes in a space-faring civilization and that focusing the enthusiasm of young people is the key to our future in space.

name: Students of Open and Universal Learning
description: The purpose of SOUL is to accelerate, experiment with, and build a stronger culture of open education at institutions of higher education, starting with MIT.

name: Sudanese@MIT
description: Sudanese@MIT is a group that focuses on connecting the MIT Sudanese community to the wider student body, Sudanese alumni, and the greater Boston/Cambridge area. We aim to create a space where Sudanese students can share their culture and connect with their peers.

name: Sundae Society
description: The purpose of Sundae Society is to spread joy and build community through a shared love of ice cream. Since our first semester, our friend group has made it a tradition to get ice cream together every two weeks to take a break from classes and reconnect. Over time, these outings have naturally grown as we’ve invited new people, creating a welcoming and social environment. We want to expand this experience to the broader campus by creating a space where students can meet new people, explore local ice cream spots, and enjoy a fun, low-pressure break from academic stress.

name: Swara
description: MIT Swara is the Indian Classical Music Group at MIT with a focus on South Indian Carnatic music. We gather weekly to jam together and learn new pieces collectively out of a shared passion for this unique style of music. We welcome people at all levels to learn and perform together, both at MIT events and at event we organize for the MIT community. Our mission is to connect musicians at MIT to each other and to the thriving Carnatic music ecosystem in the greater Boston area.

name: Syncopasian
description: Syncopasian is a co-ed a-cappella group at MIT with an emphasis on modern East Asian music. Since our founding in Spring 2008, we have put on many successful performances while supporting a vibrant and cross-cultural space for our members and audiences. Our goals as a group are as follows: (1) to sustain our musical presence by recording and producing music videos, and (2) to raise awareness for East Asian music and culture, both within MIT and the Greater Boston/Cambridge community

name: Taara
description: Taara (meaning: Star) aims to provide a dynamic platform that empowers and elevates the voices of South Asian women, femme, and gender non-conforming students at MIT. Through advocacy, activism, and action, we are committed to challenging systemic barriers that hinder our access to opportunity, representation, and well-being.

name: Tango Club
description: MIT Tango Club is dedicated to Argentine Tango. We offer classes taught by professional master instructors, made accessible to MIT students at an affordable cost. Our classes provide technique instruction that is essential for all tango dancers, and our maestros are experienced in training the body to produce an authentic quality of movement. Over time, students learn not only how to move their own bodies, but how to embrace and partner others with grace, generosity, elegance and purpose. In addition to our class schedule, the club offers access to guided practice sessions (called ”practicas")

name: Tech Catholic Community
description: Vision: A vibrant, Catholic community at MIT empowering leaders in faith and science. Mission: Welcome, Grow, Worship

name: Tech Model Railroad Club
description: The purpose of the Club shall be to increase the awareness of model railroading among M.I.T. students and other members of the M.I.T. community. The Club shall organize and administer facilities to promote the hobby and encourage the participation of the M.I.T. community.

name: Tech Squares
description: Tech Squares is a square dance and round dance group at MIT. We hold Modern Western Square Dances at the Plus level and Round dances Phase II to V once a week in addition to other events. We also hold classes to introduce beginners to square dancing.

name: Technicolor Furs
description: The purpose of the Technicolor Furs is: - To provide a welcoming environment for everyone in the MIT community to discuss, share, and participate in various aspects of the furry fandom - To promote awareness and appreciation of furries

name: Technique Yearbook
description: Founded in 1885, MIT Technique aims to provide a venue for students' creative expression through photography and design, connect student photographers with events and opportunities around campus, and document student life as part of its award-winning yearbook.

name: Technology Policy Student Society
description: In order to study and discuss issues in technology policy seminars, provide information about careers, engage in a dialogue with invited speakers, and participate in a community of open-minded students, we hereby form the Technology Policy Student Society (hereafter TPSS).

name: TechX
description: The purpose of the MIT TechX student organization is to promote knowledge of technology and of the tech industry.

name: TEDxMIT
description: The purpose of TEDxMIT is to organize and hold TEDx conferences to showcase the diverse perspectives of the MIT community. By inviting a wide variety of speakers to share their stories and talents, we hope to create an environment where students, faculty, and community members alike can learn from each other in a non-traditional setting.

name: Thai Students at MIT
description: The purpose of the Thai students at MIT is to promote understanding of the Thai heritage and interaction among Thai students. The organization provides a comfortable space for all Thai students at MIT through different seasonal and cultural activities to make the community like home. Thai students at MIT also serve as a social network of Thai students as will bring Thai students from different universities in the Boston area together through the biannual event we organize every year. .

name: The Bike Lab
description: The MIT Bike Lab is a student-run bike collective that provides services to the MIT community. Students volunteer as mechanics at weekly open hours to assist others with bike repair and maintenance. All members of the community are welcome, and access to tools and advice is completely free of charge. The shop has most of the tools needed to complete basic repairs. The club is also an opportunity for people to build community around biking and safety, and for mechanics to hold educational workshops for members of the community.

name: Traders at MIT
description: We partner with leading industry sponsors annually to host the largest intercollegiate trading competition in the country. In addition, we organize seminars and events to prepare students for successful careers in quantitative trading and finance.

name: Turkish Student Association
description: We are a group for all Turkish students and students interested in Turkish culture and Turkey. We host events pertaining to Turkish culture.

name: Ugandan Student Association
description: The purpose of the Ugandan Students Association (USA) is to promote the understanding and appreciation of Ugandan culture within the MIT community, provide a supportive network for students of Ugandan heritage, and facilitate cultural, educational, and social activities that reflect the traditions and values of Uganda.

name: UHF Repeater Assn W1XM
description: To engage with experimental radio technology in VHF, UHF, and beyond. Maintains an electrical engineering and radio-focused makerspace for MIT students to use to explore amateur radio technology and other electronics projects. Maintains the W1XM UHF repeater and the W1XM contest station, including operating the building 54 radome.

name: Ukraine@MIT
description: The purpose of Ukraine@MIT is to band together the Ukrainians of MIT and those interested in Ukrainian culture and world events.

name: Undergraduate Economics Association
description: MIT UEA optimizes the academic journey, employment prospects, and interconnectedness of MIT undergraduates within both the MIT community and the broader world.

name: Undergraduate Mathematics Association
description: The purpose of the Undergraduate Mathematics Association is to afford all MIT undergraduates the opportunity to explore mathematics, to build connections with other students and faculty who share an interest in mathematics, and to promote mathematics in the MIT community.

name: Undergraduate Research Journal
description: The mission of MURJ is to serve as a vehicle for advancing scientific communication and responsible innovation by emphasizing the intersection of science and public policy. MURJ seeks to forge a network of readers, staff, and alumni to become the next generation of STEM leaders and provide a channel to inform the world of the impact of shared science.

name: Undergraduate Research Technology Club
description: Bringing together undergraduates from around the world to present, discuss, and develop solutions to advance technology for humanity.

name: Undergraduate Society for Women in Mathematics
description: The organization aims to provide a supportive and inclusive community for woman-identifying and non-binary individuals within the MIT undergraduate math department and hosts events open to the MIT undergraduate community at large. Through regular community events and meetings, the organization will serve as a means for the aforementioned group of math students to foster relationships with one another and to share a love of mathematics. The organization will help its members to explore potential career paths and research trajectories via collaborations with various companies and research groups

name: Undergraduate Women in Physics
description: The purpose of the Undergraduate Women in Physics is to be a student-led group that supports MIT undergraduate students seeking a space to talk about the experiences of being a woman and/or being coded as a woman in physics, while acknowledging the diversity among people who have had these experiences. We sponsor community building events, share resources, and host women in STEM related events throughout the semester.

name: Vedic Vision Forum
description: Our mission is to foster holistic well-being and mindfulness among students by drawing from the timeless wisdom of spiritual philosophies. We aim to provide motivation, inspiration, and avenues for positive recreation, while encouraging personal growth through personality development and character building. Our organization is committed to guiding students away from self-destructive habits and addictions, and to nurturing principled, value-driven leaders with strong character and competence. We also seek to enrich the student experience by integrating arts, media, culture, and music into our e

name: Video Game Orchestra
description: The MIT Video Game Orchestra is a student-led ensemble dedicated to playing original arrangements of video game music, film soundtracks, and all kinds of music not usually heard in concert halls. Made up of a mix of orchestral, band, and popular instruments, we play a wide variety of genres. All our arrangements are written by members of the orchestra and are tailored for the group, and we hold workshops to help members develop their arranging and orchestration skills. Outside of rehearsal, we have lots of fun too! :) We rehearse on Sundays 2-4pm in Kresge and/or the Student Center.

name: Vietnamese Students
description: This group is to share Vietnamese cultures to MIT community.

name: Voltage
description: The mission of Voltage (collectively, the organization) is to grow and develop the electrical engineering (EE) community at MIT. We seek to advance this mission by providing a community for MIT students interested in EE, fostering hands-on engineering experience, exposing them to industry trends within EE and providing them with career advice and growth opportunities. The cornerstones of the organization are community and mentorship.

name: VR/AR at MIT
description: 1. CREATING THE VR / AR COMMUNITY. We're like-minded students, excited about VR/AR/MR. We meet and organize events for our community throughout Boston and organize the biggest Reality Hackathon in the WORLD. 2. PROVIDING RESOURCES TO DEVELOPERS We empower and provide students necessary workshops and hardware to learn and build the next generation of Virtual and Augmented Reality. 3. BRINGING INDUSTRY TO CAMPUS We bridge academia and industry by connecting students and masters. We draw from the expertise from alumni and industry champions.

name: Water Club
description: MIT Water is the premier network for water research and innovation at MIT. Our mission is to bring together creative, passionate, and motivated individuals to explore ways by which research, innovation, and policy can help solve the most pressing challenges in the water sector.

name: Weekends@MIT
description: Weekends@MIT is committed to reducing stress and facilitating student social activities while increasing health awareness and curbing dangerous behaviors at MIT.

name: WHOI Student Organization
description: The purpose of the MIT/WHOI Student Organization is to encourage interaction between MIT students and the Woods Hole community, enhance student life, elevate student voices, and advocate on behalf of the student body of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology–Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (MIT-WHOI) Joint Program. The MIT-WHOI Joint Program in Oceanography/Applied Ocean Science and Engineering is a joint venture between the two institutions to pursue excellence in oceanographic research and education. name: WMBR Radio
description: WMBR is an MIT student activity organized and operated for the benefit of the Institute and the MIT community. It is an educational FM broadcast radio station reaching beyond MIT to the greater Boston area. The two fundamental, co-existing goals of WMBR are: ● To provide MIT students with the opportunity to manage, organize, and operate an all-volunteer organization; and, ● To provide unique, innovative, quality radio programming as an alternative to that which is found on commercial radio stations. WMBR is a business incorporated in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and licensed by the federa

name: Women Business Leaders
description: MIT Women Business Leaders establishes a network of women undergraduates, faculty, alumnae and professionals to empower women in their business endeavors and support them in the development of their careers. We support our members in their personal and professional pursuits during and after their years at MIT.

name: Women in Aerospace Engineering
description: The purpose of Women in Aerospace Engineering (WAE) is to foster a community for gender minorities interested in aerospace engineering as well as encourage professional development and outreach through various social, industry, and local events.

name: Women in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
description: Our mission is to empower female and non-binary EECS students to succeed by fostering community, offering mentorship opportunities, and hosting professional development events.

name: Women's Health Research Hub
description: The purpose of Women’s Health Research Hub (WHRH) is to connect students interested in women’s health research across diverse disciplines. With no existing formal network in this rapidly rising but historically understudied field, WHRH aims to fill the gap by creating a collaborative community of medical professionals, researchers, and innovators. Our mission is to foster interdisciplinary connections, spark innovation, and promote impactful research that advances women’s health equity and outcomes. name: Women+ in Chemistry
description: Women+ in Chemistry (WIC+) is a group that uses the lens of gender to guide its support of undergraduate students, graduate students and postdoctoral scholars in the Department of Chemistry. Our mission is to foster a sense of community in the department, facilitate connections with the greater community, support the professional development of department members, and advocate for people of all genders and for gender diversity in the department and the entire chemistry community.

name: Womens Ultimate Frisbee Team
description: To advance the sport of ultimate at MIT and provide an inclusive environment in which all players are welcome to learn, develop, and lead.

name: Womens Volleyball Club
description: The MIT Women's Volleyball Club provides instructional and competitive opportunities for women of the MIT Community at all skill levels. Our mission is to provide a supportive environment for learning to excel in competition, to create a social community for club players during their time at MIT and beyond, and to connect with the greater local and regional volleyball communities through outreach and volunteer service.

name: Woop Garoo Magazine
description: To write jokes.

name: Wuming Theater Club
description: The mission of Wuming is to promote expression of Chinese culture and language through the art of theater. We aim to provide important cultural and social bonding for participating diaspora Chinese students from diverse areas of the Sinophone world, and likewise to create a community among Chinese-speaking audience members while offering them satisfying theater-going experiences. Sharing Chinese culture with non-Chinese is also a part of the mission of Wuming. We include English subtitles in the shows to encourage an inclusive audience. By doing so, we enhance diversity in the MIT community.
